newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran not interested in chemical arms - Rafsanjani.
newsitem.headline: Iran not interested in chemical arms - Rafsanjani.

text.p: Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Sunday the Islamic republic was not interested in any sort of chemical warfare and denied it was buying such weapons from China.
"This is a sheer allegation on Iran. We are not interested to be after any sort of chemical warfare or weapon," he said at a news conference in Tehran.
"We have had such a malicious experience of chemical war used by the Iraqis on us that we never use them," he said.
Rafsanjani said that during Iran's 1980-88 war with neighbouring Iraq "I witnessed such a horrible scene that I will never forget."
He said Iraqi President Saddam Hussein had resorted to advanced chemical weapons acquired from Germany.

"The chemical substance was such that for a long distance the people were harvested on the ground. Whenever there was the smell of this substance the people could not resist. It was quite horrible this scene, and I hope it will never be repeated in any country."
The United States has accused Iran of seeking to acquire weapons of mass destruction.

On Thursday, it imposed sanctions on two Chinese firms and five citizens for at least a year for allegedly transferring chemical weapons components to Tehran. Iran and China slammed the U.S. decision.
